Subject: Dedicated capacity matrix for canary vs burst prioritization

Folks —

Following up from the product/ops sync: attached is a first-pass capacity matrix that tries to map our allocation levers (reserved slots, burst lanes, per-customer canary slices, preemptible safety buffer) to the customer priority tiers Kimberly outlined. The goal: create a short decision runbook so Sales/CS can set expectations upfront and Ops can implement minimal exceptions without breaking autoscale SLOs.

High-level asks:
- Marcus/Jonas: can you confirm realistic steady-state slot counts (p50/p95) for a 3-day canary vs a 30-minute burst test? I tried to estimate on sheet 'assumptions' but need ops-validated numbers.
- Kimberly: confirm which priority band NimbleCart belongs to (they're in the pilot but asking for multi-region burst). This determines whether we give them a 1-slot canary lane or a reserved 4-slot pilot carve.
- Also we need a short autoscale-exception policy blurb: what conditions allow us to temporarily suspend the strict preemption window for a canary (e.g., <48h, non-production model, limited token budget).

I put a sample canary-vs-burst decision tree in the sheet and a diff of proposed canary policy in the patch. Please reply with numbers and any blockers. If we agree, I'd like to roll this into a lightweight runbook we can link in the pilot onboarding doc.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx; canary-policy-diff.patch
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity matrix for canary vs burst prioritization

Rachel — good framing. Quick ops reality check below.

Numbers (back-of-envelope, will validate with telemetry team by EOD):
- 3-day canary (small model, 80/20 read/write mix): p50 1.2 slots, p95 2.1 slots in us-west; add ~20% for multi-region mirroring.
- 30-minute burst (load test 10x normal): short-term p95 ~= 12 slots but can be handled by burst lane if we allow pre-warm for ~10m.

Notes and constraints:
- Autoscale exceptions we can grant: up to 48h soft reservation (mark as "canary-exempt") with a hard token cap to avoid runaway cost. Longer than 48h needs a Dedicated reservation (procurement path).
- We cannot change global preemption timing for a single customer without an explicit carve (history of noisy tenants). Any per-customer exception must be gated by a ticket and an ops-approved rollback clause.

I'll validate exact CPU/GPU footprints and update the sheet. Jonas — can you confirm whether the burst lane pre-warm API can be invoked by the pilot onboarding job? If not, we should add a one-time cron for pre-warm.

— Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-05-23T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity matrix for canary vs burst prioritization

Thanks — this looks actionable. A few product notes:

- NimbleCart classification: pilot -> "Tier B pilot with burst privileges" (they've committed to a performance test next month). That means we should default to a 1-slot canary + ability to request a 12-slot burst for test windows.
- Success criteria for canary: 95th latency under 350ms for their medium prompt mix, and <1% failure rate for the test window. If they fail the canary twice, we fall back to a longer Reserved collar conversation.
- Telemetry: we need per-request tagging so that we can retroactively attribute canary traffic vs production. Marcus — please confirm the tag name and whether it's exposed in Console traces.

On autoscale exception language: Product prefers the following simple rule in the runbook:
1) Short exception (<=48h) allowed for non-prod models and controlled token budget; Ops must be notified and can revoke if noisy.
2) Exceptions >48h require a Dedicated reservation and formal approval.

I will draft the onboarding blurb and the customer-facing language for Sales. Rachel — if you want, I can write the short paragraph for NimbleCart's MRA and include the SLOs.

— Kimberly
VP, Product (API & Platform)
